Aditya.

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: AUC plots, and model results doc
parts: Several Maxent evaluation statistic plots are viewable in the "Maxent Evaluation Plots" module of the Visualize component. You can also use the Map Prediction module to view a map of predicted area. If these don't have what you need, the Rmd file of your session can be downloaded from the Reproduce component and manipulated.

messages.subject: Re: AUC plots, and model results doc
parts:
It doesn't seem like the ROC and Omissions curves are among the outputs available in the Visualisation tab in the "Maxent Evaluation Plots" module. The Receiver Operating Curve (ROC) is a plot that helps visualise AUC (Area under the Curve), which is used to compare the portion of correctly classified known presence points, known as the sensitivity of the model, and the portion of background points that were classified as presence.

I have attached an example of an ROC curve with this message (Capture.png). I did not find this as an output in any of the visualisation modules. The downloadable data in the Save tab after running the analysis only includes the variable response curves, prediction maps, model tables, and the plots between the different evaluation parameters  (AUC diff, mtp, omission rate) vs the various regularisation parameters for each feature class. However that doesn't actually explain the performance of the model in terms of its ability to classify versus portion of background points classified as presence, as the ROC does.

You mentioned that the R code can be manipulated, could you provide some insights as to what command will help in obtaining the ROC curve? Additionally, could you help me with the code needed to get the overall maxent model output? This should also provide other outputs like the omission curve and tables that list fractional predicted areas for each cumulative threshold (have provided an example of an output doc file that MAXENT software normally provides that contains these different results that I am looking for, including the ROC curve, as an attachment).

Aditya.
